key_insight: Per-layer expert sets in MoE are largely unnecessary: a single, globally shared expert pool can replace separate per-layer experts with minimal downstream accuracy loss, decoupling depth from linear expert-parameter growth.
problem_solved: Addresses the inefficient and rigid allocation of expert capacity in Mixture-of-Experts models, where each transformer layer owns its own expert set, causing redundant parameters and poor expert utilization as models scale in depth.
method: Introduce UniPool — a globally shared expert pool that all transformer layers can route to, replacing isolated per-layer expert sets.

Use routing analyses (routing probe) to show learned top-k routing can be largely replaced (random/pooled routing yields only 1.0–1.6 point drop), motivating shared experts and simpler routing schemes.
Design capacity and balancing mechanisms for the shared pool to maintain load distribution and token-to-expert assignment across layers while preserving model throughput and memory efficiency.
impact: UniPool enables more parameter-efficient MoE scaling, reduces expert redundancy, and simplifies routing design—helping practitioners build larger, cheaper, and better-utilized expert models without sacrificing much accuracy.
visual_elements: Side-by-side diagram: traditional per-layer experts vs. UniPool global expert pool (arrows show tokens from multiple layers accessing the same experts).
Bar chart: parameter count vs. accuracy comparing per-layer MoE, UniPool, and dense baselines (highlighting similar accuracy with fewer expert parameters).
Heatmap: expert utilization across layers showing improved/more uniform usage with UniPool.
Flowchart: routing probe experiment (replace learned top-k with random routing) and measured small accuracy drop (1.0–1.6 pts) to motivate shared pooling.
paper_title: UniPool: A Globally Shared Expert Pool for Mixture-of-Experts
paper_authors: Minbin Huang, Han Shi, Chuanyang Zheng, Yimeng Wu, Guoxuan Chen
